correctness.rationale: The source supplies the finite multiplication morphism and states that general factor forms are irreducible. For m>=3, unique factorization proves that the generic fiber has exactly prod_e(mu_e!) points. The multiplication coordinates are multihomogeneous of degree one in each factor, so the ambient hyperplane pulls back to h_1+...+h_r. The projection formula therefore gives generic_degree times image_degree as the top self-intersection of this divisor, whose only surviving term has coefficient D!/prod_i(N_i!). The full reducible-locus corollary uses the source's unique maximal-dimensional component of type (d-1,1). Boundary d=2 correctly contributes the extra factor 2 from equal linear factors. The packaged checker verifies all partitions through d=10 over m=3,...,7 and several standard low-dimensional values.

value.rationale: The archival source explicitly identifies the absence of a higher-dimensional degree formula as an open natural question. Projective degree is a canonical enumerative invariant, and the theorem resolves it uniformly for every factorization type in at least three variables. The same formula immediately gives the degree of the full reducible hypersurface locus via the source's unique maximal-dimensional component. It also subsumes the known completely decomposable case while producing concrete new degrees such as 21 for reducible plane cubics of type (2,1) and 220 for reducible cubic surfaces of type (2,1). This is an exact structural answer to a literature-stated gap, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
